question: how do I do CPR on an adult
answer:
To perform CPR on an adult when someone has collapsed and is not breathing normally, follow these steps:

1. Shout for help and call 999 on speaker, placing the phone beside you [1].
2. Send someone for a defibrillator (AED) if one is nearby [1].
3. Kneel beside the person, place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest, and the other hand on top with arms straight [1].
4. Press down 5 to 6 cm, 100 to 120 times per minute (two per second), allowing the chest to come back up fully with each compression [1].
5. After 30 presses, tilt the head back, lift the chin, pinch the nose, and give two breaths, each lasting about a second, watching the chest rise [1], [3].
6. Continue with 30 presses followed by 2 breaths, repeating this cycle [1], [3].
7. If an AED arrives, turn it on and follow its voice instructions, continuing to press while the pads are applied [1], [3].
8. Do not stop until the person breathes normally on their own, a paramedic takes over, or you become exhausted [1].

Warnings: Gasping, snoring, or occasional gulps are not normal breathing; start CPR [1]. Broken ribs are common and do not mean you should stop [1].

question: salbutamol inhaler

passages.title: Salbutamol: inhaler to relieve asthma and breathlessness
Common questions about salbutamol inhalers - NHS

answer:
If you need urgent medical advice, you should call 111 [1]. For emergencies, call 999 [1].

Salbutamol inhalers are used to relieve symptoms of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) such as coughing, wheezing, and feeling breathless [2]. It works by relaxing the muscles of the airways in the lungs, making it easier to breathe [2], and provides quick relief when needed [2]. Salbutamol inhalers are called reliever inhalers [2].

You should talk to your doctor, pharmacist, or nurse if you use your salbutamol inhaler more than twice a week, as this could indicate your condition is not well controlled [2]. If you have difficulty using a salbutamol inhaler, speak to your doctor [3].
